title: Saturday Jar
genre: Hawaiian slack-key and steel-guitar ballad (island pop, 1970s Gabby Pahinui lineage)
subject: a honey seller at a Saturday farmers' table who writes a new line on the label of one jar for the same woman every week, and she buys only one jar, so he has shelves of unsent lines at home
caption: Hawaiian slack-key ballad, 1970s island sound. Slack-key guitar in open G tuning playing a thumb-bass pattern with soft hammer-ons, ukulele strumming gently on the offbeats, steel guitar sliding in long sustained notes, upright bass walking quietly, soft brushed percussion. Warm close room recording, light spring reverb on the steel guitar. Male tenor, smooth and open, clearly sung with gentle falsetto lifts. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 80 BPM, G major. Tender, hopeful, slow-sway mood. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no synth pads, no drum machine, no strings, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - slack-key guitar and steel guitar]

[Verse 1]
Saturday morning I set out the jars
Clover, wildflower, dark amber
You come by before the church bell rings nine
You hold one jar to the light

[Pre-Chorus]
I write on the label in pencil
A new line every week

[Chorus]
Saturday jar, Saturday jar
One little sentence for you
You count out your coins and you walk to your car
And you never read what I wrote

[Verse 2]
Back in my kitchen there's a shelf full of lines
The ones you never have read
Sweet as the clover and slow off the spoon
I sealed them with wax and I wait

[Pre-Chorus]
This week on the label in pencil
Your name is the very last word

[Chorus]
Saturday jar, Saturday jar
One little sentence for you
You count out your coins and you stop by your car
And this time you turn it around

[Bridge - steel guitar alone]
You asked me my name
Now there's two cups of tea on the table

[Chorus]
Saturday jar, Saturday jar
Every line was for you
Take them all home to your kitchen, my dear
And I'll bring you a fresh one on Sunday

[Outro - slack-key guitar fades]
